findings.title: File-wide fixKind check lets unsafe validated fixes bypass the portability gate
findings.what: sourceContainsNonPortableFixRegion identifies whether any fix region contains a forbidden reference, but declaresNonValidated then searches the entire source file for any manual or illustrative fixKind. A detector file containing one correctly marked manual fix and a different default-validated fix with a host path, slash command, or custom CLI therefore passes. This breaks the test's stated guarantee that every validated fix snippet is copy-paste-safe.
findings.fix: Parse each fix object and run validateFixSnippet against that fix's own snippet and fixKind, or at minimum associate each fixKind with the same syntactic fix region before deciding compliance.
findings.acceptance: Add a negative-control fixture containing two fixes in one detector source: one manual portable or non-portable fix and one separate default-validated snippet containing `claude-team`. The gate must report that source as an offender; changing the second fix to manual must make it pass.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/detectors/fix-validity.test.ts:130-153 and confirmed the mismatch: non-portability is detected from segmented fix regions, while exemption is tested with an unscoped whole-file regex. Re-read src/lib/detectors/fix-validity.ts:65-79 as comparison-only support; its per-fix validator already has the required semantics, but the source-scan gate does not invoke it.
